review.verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=incremental below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The note proves a known-cutoff minimax length rate, an explicit but one-sided unknown-cutoff nonshrinking lower regime, and oracle-order attainment only on the s=1 strong-signal face. It does not determine the critical-window length, prove that the displayed witness threshold is the true transition, or provide matching behavior between its lower and upper regimes, so the advertised frontier contribution remains a regime bracket rather than a frontier characterization. For s>1, the only new unknown-cutoff conclusion beyond the lower bound is that the proposed affine profile fails; the candidate detectable-region rate and any attaining procedure remain open. The framing generally discloses these limits, but phrases such as “proved frontier advance” should be read only as the proved one-sided barrier plus Lipschitz-face result, not as resolution of the headline joint weak-signal frontier. These unresolved central regions and the absence of an evaluated procedure outside the Lipschitz strong-signal case cap the package below a field-tier paper and constrain the projected score. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.8 < 7.2, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

review.verbatim_critique: [D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The delivered result is not the full advertised smoothness-indexed frontier: it proves the known-cutoff benchmark, a one-sided nonshrinking lower threshold for all stated smoothness levels, and oracle-order achievability only on the Lipschitz face under strong signal. The Lipschitz separated-regime result and outcome-invariant location-mixture converse nevertheless constitute a genuine field contribution, while the exact critical-window law and every positive higher-smoothness unknown-cutoff result remain open. For s>1, the note proves only that one frozen profile localizer fails, not that the proposed rate is attainable or minimax. In Theorem 3's expected-length argument, equation (18), derived on the event that the cutoff error is at most R_c, is later invoked on the larger event that the error is at most b/8; an explicit recalculation is needed to justify the asserted containment of the denominator-fallback event. The unresolved critical window, missing higher-smoothness achievability and converse term, this proof lapse, and the absence of supporting numerical evidence constrain the projected paper score despite generally faithful caveats. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.5 < 7.2, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
